# Independent expectations: compact field-library presentation

This oracle is prepared before implementation. It is a development fixture, not
generator input, a visible Field document, or evidence that any test has passed.
It complements `EXPECTED.md`; its synthetic identities, coverage, selection and
topology expectations remain intact. No test is run by preparing this file.

## Basis and scope

The accepted high-frequency-surface and model-optimization 3DGS examples establish
the presentation baseline: short linked timeline titles, adjacent explanations,
and paper leaves with one method sentence and usable navigation. Their scientific
facts, corpus sizes, exact coordinates and pixel heights are not generic limits.
These expectations concern visible output, independently of the sizing algorithm.

## Required structure and content placement

- Keep the full 01 list and the distinct 02 timeline, 03 technical-route and 04
  challenge/solution views, with their required paired Markdown and editable Canvas.
  Preserve the declared per-view selection, every required semantic node, paper
  occurrence, role, connection, owner and source. A representative 02 selection
  does not erase papers from the complete list or another required view.
- Keep the five 01 columns: `论文资料`, `年份与发表`, `研究线索`,
  `原 PDF · ZotFlow`, `分析与图示`. Put complete publication metadata in the
  publication column or linked paper record, rather than adding diagnostic columns.
- A 02 paper title contains a linked short name and compact year/date label only.
  A necessary identity disambiguator may be part of the short name. Its adjacent
  explanation contains one or two sentences about the change and relevant tradeoff,
  plus a working detail/source link. Complete first-preprint dates, venue lines and
  extra source-button rows do not belong inside the title card.
- A 03/04 paper leaf contains one linked paper title, one specific method sentence,
  and the available paper/material, analysis, paper-Canvas and original-source
  navigation. Keep conditions, costs, limitations and detailed evidence in the
  appropriate branch/solution node or paired prose, reachable from that leaf.
  An item-specific coverage exception may remain a short readable label.
- Preserve scientific explanations, relation reasons, inputs, conditions and source
  evidence when removing repetition. Do not make compactness depend on omitting
  papers, merging distinct methods, weakening topology or deleting evidence.

## Availability and human navigation

For a common state such as "full analyses and paper analysis Canvases have not been
created", one readable statement in 01 or a linked coverage ledger is sufficient;
each relevant view must make that statement easy to reach. Do not repeat a long
missing-analysis message in every title, explanation and paper leaf. Keep an
item-specific missing original, abstract-only coverage or unavailable source
visible in its list row or paper record, with a short leaf indication when needed
to avoid a misleading source action. An available analysis still has its actual
link; an absent analysis never gains a fabricated note, Canvas, button or success
label. A missing source cannot be hidden by a collection-wide statement.

The human Field tree contains its research views, paper records and supplied
human-readable source material. Test plans,
acceptance logs, machine inputs and execution diagnostics remain outside that
human research tree. Do not add development-only navigation nodes or copy this
oracle into the Field. Audit evidence can be retained in the development workspace
without appearing as research content.

## Bounded positive and negative cases

| Case | Expected positive result | Failure example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Timeline title | `[[paper-a/Paper|Method A · YYYY ↗]]`, followed by a separate concise explanation and detail/source link | A title card adds full first-preprint date, venue, source-button row and repeated coverage warning |
| Distinct identities | Similar short names retain a supplied author/variant disambiguator and their correct owners | Shortening makes two distinct papers appear to share an identity or source |
| Paper leaf | Linked title, one concrete prepared method sentence, then only usable navigation or a necessary short availability label | The leaf repeats the branch's input, gain, cost and limitation paragraphs, or gains a "main modules" section |
| Common missing analysis | A reachable readable ledger states the shared missing state; existing material/source links remain usable | Every leaf repeats "analysis not generated; paper diagram not generated", or an absent analysis is shown as available |
| One missing original | That paper's row/record visibly says the original is unavailable; other originals remain linked | A general coverage paragraph conceals the exception, or another paper's PDF is reused |
| Different evidence coverage | Supplied full-fragment, abstract-only and unknown states remain distinguishable in reachable records | Compact prose invents method details for an unknown item or treats an abstract as full-paper support |
| Required repeated occurrence | A paper required by different challenges keeps each distinct leaf occurrence and the same owner | Deduplication removes a required leaf to reduce diagram size |
| Long mixed-language label | A prepared CJK/Latin title wraps, preserves its identity and full text, and expands only as needed | Clipping, ellipsis, a fixed height, or added metadata used to compensate for poor sizing |
| Source destination | Long URLs, query strings and parentheses remain byte-preserved; visible link labels wrap as needed | Break characters alter a destination, a hidden URL is displayed as extra title prose, or a source link is dropped |
| Companion prose | A relation reason and its source remain readable at the relevant discussion point | The same method or limitation sentence is duplicated within a paragraph or reproduced as a second boilerplate section |
| Field contents | Only the requested views, paper records, human-readable source material and their research navigation are visible | Test instructions, machine-input files or acceptance diagnostics appear in the research tree |

These cases use supplied synthetic text and declared structure. They do not impose
a scientific paper quota, a topic-specific branch count, or one universal card size.

## Native appearance and completion

Check the affected view in native Obsidian with its intended shipped style enabled.
The timeline uses effective 22px title text and 19px description text; radial body
text uses effective 18px text. Inspect computed heading/link size and actual padding
where relevant: setting a container's font size alone does not prove a theme has
not enlarged its headings. Dedicated display headers keep their separate treatment.

Each card must fit its rendered text and links, leave approximately one rendered
text line of spare click space, and remain legible at a normal reading zoom. Verify
the content and final link are visible, scrolling is not needed to reveal clipped
content, and the space beneath the final content is usable. Long labels may require
taller cards; an exact exemplar height is not an acceptance requirement.

Geometry/schema checks do not establish native font size, click space or working
navigation. Human review remains pending until the user confirms the affected
appearance and representative detail/source clicks. Structural completion does
not establish scientific support, full-paper analysis or installed-product acceptance.
